note: Spent 3 hours debugging a weird race condition in our LangGraph interrupt state saver. Turned out SqliteSaver needs check_same_thread=False when using multi-threaded Typer CLI commands. Fixed it and test pass rate jumped from 82% to 100%.
Refactored some agent code today. It feels much cleaner and better organized now.
Woke up late, drank 2 cups of coffee, answered emails. Didn't write any code or build any features today.

Benchmarked our LLM router between Groq llama-3.3-70b and Anthropic Claude 3.5 Sonnet. Groq served requests in 210ms vs 850ms for Claude, while maintaining a 94% score on our voice alignment rubric across 50 test notes.

Built a timezone-aware slot policy in Postwright converting audience timezones to Africa/Nairobi. Added DST handling using Python zoneinfo module. See full details at https://github.com/example/postwright/pull/42 for the implementation details.

Implemented exponential backoff retries and token cost tracking for Groq and Gemini API calls in Postwright. Now rate limits (429) automatically retry with a 30s timeout and track total wait time per run.

Debugging session log:
1. Problem: State checkpointer was throwing operational database locked errors under parallel evaluation runs.
2. Root cause: SQLite WAL mode was not enabled for the checkpoint database connection pool.
3. Fix: Added PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL; on database initialization.
4. Result: Zero locking errors across 100 concurrent pipeline runs and throughput increased by 3.5x.
5. Lessons: Always check SQLite PRAGMA settings when building local multi-threaded agent tools.
Fixed a minor typo in the README.md file.
Migrated from Pydantic v1 to Pydantic v2 model definitions across all 12 core state schemas in Postwright. Serialization overhead dropped from 45ms to 8ms per graph transition.

Added LangSmith tracing configuration via env vars (LANGCHAIN_TRACING_V2=true). Ensured zero API keys are logged to stdout by sanitizing config metadata in Typer CLI output. Read the docs at https://docs.smith.langchain.com for details.
Tested our critic evaluation node on 20 rough build notes. The critic caught 14 posts with missing concrete metrics and forced revision loops until quality scores exceeded 14/20.
Just played around with some prompt engineering techniques for structured outputs.
Created an independent LLM-as-judge harness comparing Groq and Gemini evaluations. Found a +1.4 score bias in the in-pipeline critic, prompting a suggested threshold bump from 14 to 15.
Integrated uv for dependency management in our Python 3.12 workspace. Cold setup time dropped from 28s to 1.2s across CI pipeline steps.
Explored adding Rust extensions to speed up graph state serialization, but decided against it to maintain a pure Python codebase as mandated by project requirements.

Discovered that rate limit 429 errors were causing full pipeline restarts during eval suite runs. Implemented a resumable progress saver (evals/.eval_progress.json) so --resume picks up right where it stopped.
Added PR diff generation for human review node edits. When a human edits a draft, unified_diff is recorded in SQLite approval_history table with score and cost.
